title: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists

tasks.short: Analyse customer characteristics and buying behaviour to identify markets and demand drivers.

steps.what: Define customer segments, demand questions and permitted data use.
Export customer records, purchases and campaign responses from source systems.
Join records, remove duplicates and check missing or inconsistent fields.
Compare segments, purchase cohorts, repeat buying and seasonal demand.
Assess potential markets and distinguish demand explanations from observed associations.
Review opportunities and select a market hypothesis for validation.

tasks.design: Scheduled, minimised extracts from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} form a governed customer dataset on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic joins, quality checks and configured cohort views in the {BI} expose demand patterns; the analyst interprets opportunities in the {DOCS} before the manager selects validation work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer identifiers, definitions and access differed across systems. Repeated exports and workbook joins consumed time before analysis could begin.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data pipelines and configured analytical views cover the structured workload. AI-assisted coding reduces development effort without requiring a model to calculate results.
tasks.still_hard: Missing demographics, shared accounts and unmatched purchases limit segment accuracy. Observational purchase patterns do not establish why demand changed or reveal all potential customers.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise selection bias, connect behaviour with market context and choose evidence that could disprove an attractive opportunity.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one emerging segment-demand hypothesis for validation.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time joining exports and more time investigating demand changes. Proposed delegation lets the analyst choose diagnostic cuts and validation proposals; the manager retains targeting and investment decisions.

reach.task: Use cohort evidence to propose assortment tests.
reach.learn: Product economics, stock constraints and controlled assortment experiments.

evidence.claim: Deterministic joins, cohort calculations and configured dashboards can handle structured customer-demand analysis.
Aggregate analysis still needs controls for identity matching, missing data and observational bias.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The initial scope uses existing customer attributes and transactions rather than inferred sensitive characteristics.
GDPR purpose limitation, minimisation, access and retention controls apply to customer data.
The design supports aggregate research and does not execute individual targeting, pricing or exclusion.
The mostly structured inputs justify deterministic analysis; no model loop is needed initially.
Shared datasets and definitions support the reporting and market-positioning tasks.
The digest provides no direct customer-demand analytics implementation case.
unknowns: Whether source systems share reliable customer identifiers.
Which demographic attributes exist and may lawfully be used.
Whether transaction history includes returns, channel changes and offline purchases.
Which analytical features are available in the existing {BI}.
Whether the implementation triggers consultation under national rules.
research_questions: How much does unmatched transaction data change segment rankings?
Which demand patterns survive changes in segment definitions and observation windows?
Which proposed demand drivers can be tested through controlled experiments?
new_work: Resolve unmatched records and investigate data-quality alerts.
Maintain segment definitions, joins and deletion propagation.
Review dashboard coverage when channels or source systems change.
Check access, aggregation thresholds and retention settings.
Track which opportunity hypotheses were validated or rejected.
tasks.statement: Collect and analyze data on customer demographics, preferences, needs, and buying habits to identify potential markets and factors affecting product demand.

tasks.short: Prepare research reports with charts, written findings and recommendations.

steps.what: Gather approved datasets, research notes and the reporting brief.
Reconcile definitions, periods and totals in an analysis workbook.
Build charts and tables for the report.
Explain findings, limitations and possible implications in a report draft.

loop.input: Validated tables, chart metadata, research notes and reporting brief.
loop.output: Report draft linking each factual claim to a source or table.
loop.check: Check numbers against tables and source references against the source pack; analyst checks interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; unresolved claims remain flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but explaining mixed findings and limitations requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Review conclusions and approve the report for its intended audience.
Circulate the approved report and archive its supporting material.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles approved data, checks totals and feeds chart templates in the {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a source-linked report in the {DOCS}; approval releases the report through the {WORKFLOW} and {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data definitions differed, chart preparation was repetitive, and narrative templates handled changing findings poorly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing chart exports and deterministic checks cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while bounded drafting handles prose.
tasks.still_hard: Weak samples, conflicting evidence and causal interpretation still require research judgement. Source links alone do not prove that conclusions follow.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a persuasive story exceeds the evidence and explain what a decision maker can safely conclude.

ambition.what: Decision briefs showing which evidence would change a campaign recommendation.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time formatting and more time testing explanations. Proposed delegation lets the analyst choose follow-up analyses; the marketing manager retains release and spending decisions.

reach.task: Shape research findings into clear executive briefs.
reach.learn: Audience structure, claim editing and concise explanations of uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Data checks, reusable chart templates and document assembly can automate recurring report preparation.
Source verification needs explicit controls: the digest documents a report containing nonexistent citations.

assumptions: Steps describe a recurring internal report in a mid-size European marketing team.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
An existing reporting template and stable metric definitions cover recurring reports.
Distribution is internal; external publication requires a separate release action.
Build ranges assume existing data access routes and exclude major source-system replacement.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; the proposed design does not require employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which reports recur and how much their structure changes.
Whether the {BI} supports usable chart and dataset exports.
Who may approve reports and which recipients may access source data.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the actual implementation.
research_questions: Which report sections can use fixed templates without losing meaning?
How often do reviewers change the interpretation rather than the wording?
Can every numerical claim be checked against a versioned table?
new_work: Review flagged data exceptions and unsupported narrative claims.
Maintain metric definitions, report templates and source references.
Check chart rendering and permissions after source changes.
Sample approved reports for misleading interpretation.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports of findings, illustrating data graphically and translating complex findings into written text.

tasks.short: Run customer and employee satisfaction research, assess results, and agree improvement priorities.

steps.what: Agree satisfaction measures, confidentiality promises, and decisions the research should support.
Export the eligible customer audience and contact preferences.
Prepare the eligible employee audience using approved organisational groupings.
Configure questions, routing, reporting groups, and invitation text in a survey platform.
Approve invitations, privacy safeguards, and any required employee consultation.
Send invitations and scheduled reminders through the survey platform.
Clean responses, calculate scores, and compare permitted groups and previous waves.
Read comments and group expressed concerns without identifying individual respondents.

loop.input: Minimised comments with direct identifiers removed and approved theme definitions.
loop.output: Draft themes, supporting passages, and ambiguous comments.
loop.check: Enforce disclosure rules; analyst checks theme meaning, rare cases, and identifying passages.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction; ambiguous comments stay unclassified for human handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments express similar concerns in varied language that keyword rules miss.

steps.what: Interpret findings with stakeholders and agree improvement priorities.
Prepare and publish an aggregate satisfaction report for authorised audiences.

tasks.design: Configure invitations and reminders in the survey platform in {OTHER}, using restricted audience connectors from {CRM} and {HCM}. Deterministic scoring and disclosure rules on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feed {BI}; a bounded loop proposes comment themes for analyst review. A report template in {DOCS} uses approved aggregates and priorities agreed in a human discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audience lists, survey exports, and scoring workbooks were separate. Confidential comments and small groups made unattended reporting difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing survey features handle distribution, while deterministic connectors and scoring remove repeated exports and calculations. Bounded text classification can assist comment review without assigning individual employee scores.
tasks.still_hard: Nonresponse bias, anonymity, reidentification, and trust remain difficult. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation depends on national rules, and employee evaluation would require a separate assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what respondents are reluctant to say, challenge convenient interpretations, and secure credible action from leaders.

ambition.what: A quarterly customer satisfaction priority review using a stable comparison series.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time moving responses and calculating scores, and more time testing explanations and following up priorities. The analyst can gain authority to convene a priority review when agreed aggregate measures deteriorate.

reach.task: Choose customer experience improvements supported by satisfaction evidence.
reach.learn: Service ownership, customer retention economics, and practical intervention design.

reach.task: Design confidential employee listening and communicate resulting actions.
reach.learn: Employee trust, disclosure control, and consultation under national rules.

evidence.claim: Survey distribution, score calculations, and aggregate dashboards can use configuration and deterministic code.
Comment theme classification needs human review and controls against identifying respondents.
The EU AI Act identifies worker evaluation as a high-risk use; ordinary aggregate satisfaction research needs its own use assessment.
Dutch national rules include works council consent concerning employee data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: Customer and employee studies are separate branches; each uses its relevant audience source.
The employee study reports aggregate expressed views and does not infer emotions or evaluate individuals.
Identity and reminder status are kept separate from analysis data where the confidentiality design requires it.
Reporting groups and suppression thresholds are approved before collection.
The low-drudgery prior remains plausible: trust and interpretation occupy substantial human time.
The access range includes privacy review and applicable employee consultation; national procedures can extend it.
unknowns: What confidentiality promises have already been made to respondents?
Which lawful bases, retention periods, and processing arrangements apply?
Which employee consultation requirements apply in the operating countries?
Can the survey platform separate contact records from response data?
Who approves disclosure thresholds and improvement priorities?
research_questions: Which existing exports and calculations can be eliminated through survey configuration?
How often do proposed themes conceal minority concerns or reveal respondents?
Are repeated waves comparable enough to support a quarterly customer review?
new_work: Review themes, ambiguous comments, and disclosure risks.
Maintain audience eligibility, scoring definitions, and suppression rules.
Monitor nonresponse and changes in survey composition.
Manage deletion schedules and access to response data.
Track whether agreed satisfaction priorities lead to action.
tasks.statement: Measure and assess customer and employee satisfaction.

tasks.short: Track market and sales trends, produce forecasts and explain changes in the outlook.

steps.what: Agree forecast horizon, market segments and planning assumptions.
Retrieve sales history, pipeline and indicators from a market data service.
Align periods, currencies and segments; investigate missing values and unusual movements.
Calculate trends and seasonal forecasts, comparing methods against historical outcomes.
Challenge assumptions and agree an outlook with downside and upside scenarios.
Publish the approved forecast and trend charts for planning teams.
Compare actual sales with archived forecasts and flag persistent errors.

tasks.design: Integrations bring sales from the {ERP}, pipeline from the {CRM} and licensed market indicators from the {OTHER} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Scheduled statistical code validates data, compares forecasts with historical outcomes and prepares scenarios; approved versions feed the {BI}. Forecast errors trigger review, while changes to planning assumptions require the marketing manager's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring exports, changing segment definitions and spreadsheet formulas made refreshes fragile. Market indicator licences could also restrict reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard statistical methods and scheduled data checks already cover the calculation work. AI-assisted coding can make source adapters and validation cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: New products, structural breaks and sparse markets weaken historical forecasts. Statistical intervals do not cover every commercial shock.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when historical patterns no longer apply and connect market evidence with commercial developments.

ambition.what: Weekly review of demand scenarios for priority market segments

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding workbooks and more time examining demand risks and forecast failures. Authority to approve the planning outlook does not change.

reach.task: Adjust the timing of market launches using demand scenarios.
reach.learn: Forecast calibration, launch economics and the cost of acting too early or late.

evidence.claim: Trend calculations, statistical forecasting, historical validation and error monitoring can run without a language model.
Human review remains useful for structural changes and commercial assumptions outside the historical data.

assumptions: Today uses recurring system exports and spreadsheet-based forecasting.
The pilot covers established segments with enough comparable history for validation.
Candidate forecasts fail closed when data or validation checks fail.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Aggregated commercial data is sufficient; employee monitoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Historical depth, restatements and segment consistency.
Market data licence terms and export access.
Current forecast accuracy and the business cost of errors.
Whether source records require additional GDPR controls or consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which statistical baselines work reliably for sparse or intermittent demand?
Which licensed indicators have stable historical vintages suitable for forecast validation?
new_work: Investigate missing feeds, unusual values and validation failures.
Review forecast drift and compare against simple baselines.
Maintain segment mappings, indicator licences and archived forecast versions.
Document assumption changes and scenario overrides.
tasks.statement: Forecast and track marketing and sales trends, analyzing collected data.

tasks.short: Gather and interpret evidence about the company's market position.

steps.what: Agree the market, comparison group and positioning question.
Retrieve sales, pipeline and campaign performance for the agreed market.
Gather competitor offers and market estimates from websites and market databases.

loop.input: Documents and permitted website captures from an approved source list.
loop.output: Dated evidence records with quoted passages, units, geography and source references.
loop.check: Validate fields and quoted passages against captures; analyst checks ambiguous definitions and coverage.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document within the approved batch; inaccessible sources go to an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed feeds handle structured figures, but offer descriptions and market definitions vary across documents.

steps.what: Align currencies, periods, categories and comparison coverage in a workbook.
Assess relative strengths, gaps and uncertainty in a positioning brief.
Discuss implications and agree which positioning assumptions need testing.

tasks.design: Approved feeds from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} join a dated evidence register on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop reads permitted market documents, while deterministic comparison rules feed the {BI}; the analyst uses those comparisons to prepare a positioning brief in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Market definitions rarely matched internal categories, and public evidence required repeated reading and manual recording.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors and reusable mappings reduce collection work. Bounded extraction can capture evidence from varied documents without delegating source selection or strategic conclusions.
tasks.still_hard: Private competitor performance is often unavailable. Estimated market sizes and mismatched definitions can make precise rankings misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a useful competitive frame and distinguish a real market disadvantage from a measurement gap.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on which competitive positioning assumption to test next.

tasks.altitude: The analyst shifts from repeated collection to investigating meaningful changes. Proposed delegation lets the analyst prioritise evidence gaps within the agreed research scope; the manager approves positioning changes.

reach.task: Choose positioning hypotheses for campaign tests.
reach.learn: Competitive framing, commercial trade-offs and testable positioning claims.

evidence.claim: Scheduled data collection, explicit comparison mappings and dashboards support recurring market-position analysis.
Extracting evidence from varied market documents needs source checks and exception handling.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The comparison covers an agreed set of markets and competitors.
Collection uses permitted access, licensed data or approved public sources.
External evidence is mainly organisational or aggregate data; personal data receives GDPR controls.
The digest provides no direct market-positioning implementation case.
Shared commercial extracts and market datasets can also support the other tasks; build ranges are not additive.
unknowns: Which market databases are licensed and permit automated retrieval.
Whether credible market denominators exist for the chosen segments.
How internal categories map to external market definitions.
Whether relevant access or national consultation requirements extend the schedule.
research_questions: Which comparisons remain useful when market-share denominators are unavailable?
How often do source definitions or competitor offers change?
Which apparent market changes disappear after adjusting for coverage?
new_work: Review ambiguous extracted evidence and missing sources.
Maintain source permissions, comparison mappings and capture schedules.
Investigate stale estimates and changes in market definitions.
Record why a positioning conclusion changed.
tasks.statement: Seek and provide information to help companies determine their position in the marketplace.

tasks.short: Measure campaign results, assess the strength of the evidence and recommend changes.

steps.what: Agree campaign objectives, comparison periods, outcome measures and decision thresholds.
Export campaign, web analytics, lead and revenue results.
Reconcile campaign identifiers, dates, spend, conversions and duplicate records.
Calculate agreed performance measures and compare results with baselines.
Assess attribution limits, confounding factors and whether results support causal claims.
Write findings, limitations and proposed campaign changes.

loop.input: Validated campaign metric table and analyst's effectiveness assessment.
loop.output: Draft report with metric references, limitations and proposed changes.
loop.check: Verify every number against the metric table; analyst checks recommendations and causal wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unresolved claims are omitted and flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template covers tables, but varied findings and qualifications need prose adapted to the evidence.

steps.what: Review findings and approve campaign changes or further experiments.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations load approved data from the {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {CRM}, {ERP} and web analytics in the {OTHER} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks feed the {BI}; a bounded drafting loop turns validated results and the analyst's assessment into a report in the {DOCS}. The analyst approves the report, and the marketing manager approves campaign changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign identifiers, conversion definitions and revenue timing differ across systems. Connecting them has required recurring manual reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting features handle measures, while small coded adapters and checks can make reconciliation repeatable. Bounded drafting can use approved tables and assessment notes.
tasks.still_hard: Missing consented tracking, delayed sales and weak experiments limit attribution. More frequent reporting cannot establish causation by itself.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful outcomes, challenge misleading comparisons and decide which uncertainty matters for a spending decision.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of the next campaign experiment

tasks.altitude: The analyst replaces much of the reporting cycle with experiment design and evidence review. Campaign spending approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Choose the next budget allocation experiment.
reach.learn: Incrementality, experiment power, channel constraints and marginal return.

evidence.claim: Data joins, metric calculations and refresh checks can be deterministic; causal interpretation needs research judgement.
A documented report case involved invented citations and a partial refund, supporting source checks on generated reports.

assumptions: Today combines exports and spreadsheet reconciliation with an existing reporting view in the {BI}.
The pilot covers a limited channel set and one agreed conversion definition.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Only permitted data is joined; identified customer records are unnecessary for most reporting.
unknowns: Availability and consistency of campaign and conversion identifiers.
Existing attribution methods, experiments and reporting licences.
Data access, tracking permissions and retention requirements.
Whether employee-level reporting triggers consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which documented marketing measurement cases separate reporting savings from improved causal evidence?
Which source interfaces expose stable identifiers and historical corrections?
new_work: Resolve rejected joins, missing feeds and changed conversion definitions.
Review generated findings and unsupported causal language.
Maintain connector mappings, metric tests and access permissions.
Check experiments for contamination and delayed outcomes.
tasks.statement: Measure the effectiveness of marketing, advertising, and communications programs and strategies.

tasks.short: Research consumer opinions and marketing strategies with research and marketing colleagues.

steps.what: Agree research questions and intended marketing decisions with colleagues.
Draft the sample plan, questionnaire and interview guide.

loop.input: Research brief, approved questions, protocol template and recruitment constraints.
loop.output: Draft questionnaire and interview guide within a completed protocol template.
loop.check: Validate required sections and routing; analyst checks leading questions, accessibility and fit to the research question.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision against a checklist; unresolved design choices go to the statistician.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing questions are reused first; new concepts require context-sensitive wording and follow-up prompts.

steps.what: Review sampling, question design and analysis limits before fieldwork.
Invite eligible participants and coordinate interview appointments.
Monitor survey responses and recruitment gaps in the survey platform.
Interview participants and record research notes.
Clean responses, code open answers and calculate study results.

loop.input: Minimised open answers and approved coding definitions.
loop.output: Proposed codes with supporting text spans and an uncertain category.
loop.check: Validate allowed codes and text spans; analyst checks a sample and all ambiguous or novel responses. Statistics run deterministically.
loop.stop: One classification pass per response; ambiguous responses go to manual coding without repeated guessing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured answers use fixed rules, but varied open answers express the same meaning in different words.

steps.what: Interpret findings with colleagues and agree marketing hypotheses for testing.

tasks.design: An approved protocol in the {DOCS} drives participant invitations through the {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, with survey-platform response feeds entering the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks calculate results, and a bounded loop proposes open-answer codes for review; interviews and joint interpretation stay with researchers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research design and interviews were mixed with invitation chasing, response cleaning and manual coding. Open answers resisted fixed keyword rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing survey configuration handles routing and monitoring. Small custom integrations and bounded text classification can reduce coordination and coding work.
tasks.still_hard: Recruiting a representative sample, asking neutral questions and interpreting what participants leave unsaid remain difficult. A coding model cannot repair a biased study.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, notice hesitation, probe unexpected answers and challenge colleagues' preferred explanations.

ambition.what: Research with low-frequency customers who are usually absent from feedback studies.

tasks.altitude: Researchers spend more time on recruitment quality, interviews and study interpretation. Proposed delegation lets the analyst adjust recruitment within approved sample rules; protocol changes return to the statistician.

reach.task: Translate consumer language into search-intent hypotheses.
reach.learn: Search-intent grouping, query evidence and experiment design.

evidence.claim: Survey routing, invitation scheduling and response monitoring can use existing software configuration.
Bounded text coding can assist qualitative analysis when codes, supporting text and human checks are explicit.

assumptions: The task covers a mixed survey and interview study; some studies use only one method.
Shares describe workflow effort across contributing roles, excluding participant completion time.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
A statistician is available internally or as an external specialist.
Participant contact, data processing and retention have an appropriate GDPR basis; marketing permission is not assumed to cover research.
Research access and privacy review are included in the access range. Employee studies may also require consultation under national rules.
The design uses no workplace emotion recognition or automated individual eligibility decisions.
unknowns: Whether studies include employees, children or sensitive personal data.
Which participant contact and recruitment permissions exist.
Whether the survey platform supports response exports and scheduling.
Which national rules and consultation arrangements apply.
Which languages and accessibility needs the study must support.
research_questions: Which open-answer codes have acceptable agreement between independent human reviewers?
Which recruitment channels systematically miss the intended new group?
Does assisted questionnaire drafting increase leading or repetitive questions?
new_work: Review invitation batches, recruitment exceptions and participant withdrawals.
Audit suggested codes against human coding and update coding guidance.
Maintain survey routing, integrations and retention settings.
Check that emerging themes are not lost through fixed categories.
Review protocol changes and any required employee consultation.
tasks.statement: Conduct research on consumer opinions and marketing strategies, collaborating with marketing professionals, statisticians, pollsters, and other professionals.

tasks.short: Present market evidence and commercial proposals to management, then capture agreed decisions.

steps.what: Gather approved findings, forecasts and product economics for the management agenda.
Develop promotion, distribution, design or pricing options and assess trade-offs.
Prepare a concise briefing with recommendations, supporting evidence and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Analyst's commercial options and approved evidence pack with source references.
loop.output: Draft briefing with options, recommendation, trade-offs and open questions.
loop.check: Match numbers and references to supplied sources; analyst checks recommendation fidelity and omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unsupported statements are removed and unresolved sections return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Charts can use templates, but a concise argument across varied commercial options needs adapted prose.

steps.what: Present proposals, answer challenges and explore management concerns.
Approve next steps, action owners and any required escalation.
Copy agreed decisions into a separate action list.

tasks.design: A generator assembles approved evidence from the {BI}, {ERP} and {DOCS}, then a bounded drafting loop prepares a briefing for analyst approval. Managers record decisions and action owners once in the {PROJECT}, whose action view replaces the separate follow-up list. Live discussion and commercial approval remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was spread across reports, and briefing preparation depended on manual copying and rewriting. Meeting notes and action lists duplicated decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and data links can assemble evidence consistently. A bounded loop can draft from approved material, while one structured decision record removes duplicate paperwork.
tasks.still_hard: Product economics may be disputed or incomplete. Management alignment, confidential pricing choices and cross-functional commitments still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Read concerns in the room, explain uncertainty and negotiate a decision that affected teams can carry out.

ambition.what: A short commercial options clinic for product teams before management review

tasks.altitude: Preparation takes less of the week, leaving time to test proposals with product teams before the meeting. Management decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Frame a pricing or distribution proposal for management approval.
reach.learn: Unit economics, channel incentives and how approval authority is delegated.

evidence.claim: Approved-source briefing generation and a shared decision record can reduce preparation and duplicate recording.
A documented report case involving invented sources supports checking generated briefing references before use.

assumptions: Today involves manual briefing preparation and a separate follow-up list.
Approved findings and forecasts are available with source references.
The pilot uses written decision entries rather than meeting recording or transcription.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Who can approve pricing, distribution and product changes.
Whether evidence can be accessed without copying confidential source records.
Whether the existing {PROJECT} can hold both decisions and action views.
Whether intended processing requires employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which briefing evaluations reliably detect omitted qualifications and unsupported recommendations?
Which existing record features support linked decisions and actions without duplicate entry?
new_work: Review briefing claims, references and confidential details.
Maintain briefing templates and links to approved evidence.
Keep decision owners, due dates and escalation routes current.
Remove superseded briefing versions from active circulation.
tasks.statement: Attend staff conferences to provide management with information and proposals concerning the promotion, distribution, design, and pricing of company products or services.

tasks.short: Collect competitor evidence and compare prices, sales signals, marketing, and distribution.

steps.what: Define competitors, comparable offers, markets, and evidence requirements.
Collect public prices and offer details through a web browser.
Read reports and marketing material for sales signals and distribution methods.

loop.input: Approved competitor reports and marketing material with source dates.
loop.output: Sales signals, channel descriptions, and positioning claims with supporting passages.
loop.check: Require source identifiers and exact passages; analyst checks attribution and separates reported facts from estimates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per document; unsupported fields remain unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Channel descriptions and sales commentary vary across prose documents and lack stable fields.

steps.what: Copy evidence into a comparison workbook and standardise units and categories.
Calculate comparable price differences and chart changes over time.
Check surprising changes, missing evidence, and misleading offer comparisons.
Discuss implications for positioning, pricing, and channel choices.
Assemble and circulate the competitor brief to internal stakeholders.

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collect permitted price sources and store dated evidence; a bounded loop extracts observations from documents in {DOCS}. Deterministic comparison rules feed {BI}, while the analyst checks exceptions and discusses implications. A template assembles the validated brief and {EMAIL} distributes it internally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competitor sources used inconsistent formats, and comparable offers needed manual reconciliation. Private sales figures were often unavailable.
tasks.enabler_now: Feed ingestion, stored snapshots, and comparison code are established techniques that AI coding can assemble faster. Bounded extraction helps with prose while preserving evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Collection permissions, changing pages, geographic prices, bundles, taxes, and promotional conditions complicate comparisons. Actual competitor sales often remain unknown.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real competitive change from a different bundle, audience, or reporting convention.

ambition.what: A weekly competitor-response recommendation for the campaign planning meeting.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time copying prices and more time investigating meaningful changes. The analyst can gain authority to trigger a positioning review; pricing decisions remain with the commercial owner.

reach.task: Adjust positioning when competitor offers change.
reach.learn: Margin constraints, customer value, and evidence thresholds for changing a campaign.

reach.task: Compare product bundles and promotional prices.
reach.learn: Unit economics, delivery charges, tax treatment, and product equivalence.

evidence.claim: Dated price collection, unit normalisation, and dashboards can use deterministic technology.
Extracting competitor observations from prose needs source checks and analyst review.
The digest records a report containing nonexistent sources, illustrating the need for evidence validation.

assumptions: The initial build covers a bounded competitor list and permitted sources.
Structured feeds or stable page fields cover most price collection.
Unsupported pages enter an exception queue rather than an autonomous browsing process.
Competitor sales estimates remain labelled separately from disclosed sales.
The gathering prior fits this task, but commercial interpretation remains human.
Only public business evidence is collected; personal data requires a separate GDPR assessment.
unknowns: Which sources permit automated collection and historical storage?
How many markets, currencies, and offer variants must be compared?
Which competitor sales figures are actually available?
Who may trigger a positioning review?
What source subscriptions and access costs already exist?
research_questions: Which sources support stable, permitted collection without browser maintenance?
Which comparison rules prevent false price-change alerts?
How often does extracted channel evidence need substantive correction?
new_work: Repair connectors when source formats change.
Review extracted observations and comparison exceptions.
Maintain offer matching, tax, currency, and unit rules.
Track source permissions, freshness, and missing sales evidence.
tasks.statement: Gather data on competitors and analyze their prices, sales, and method of marketing and distribution.

tasks.short: Track industry statistics, read trade literature, and identify relevant market trends.

steps.what: Select trusted industry sources, indicators, and topics to monitor.
Check statistical releases and new publications through a web browser.
Read trade literature and record relevant findings with citations.

loop.input: New licensed or public articles and reports within the monitoring scope.
loop.output: Draft findings with source dates, exact passages, and uncertainty notes.
loop.check: Verify source identifiers and passage matches; analyst checks context and unsupported conclusions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per document within a configured document limit; failures enter a reading queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant findings occur in varied prose and cannot be reliably captured by numeric fields or keywords.

steps.what: Transfer published statistics into an indicator workbook with dates and definitions.
Calculate indicator changes and prepare charts against comparable periods.
Assess relevance, conflicting evidence, and implications for the business.
Assemble charts, findings, and citations into the industry bulletin.
Circulate the bulletin to the agreed internal audience.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieve permitted releases, preserve revisions, and calculate indicators for {BI}. A bounded loop prepares cited literature notes in {DOCS}, which the analyst reviews before deciding business relevance. A deterministic template assembles the approved bulletin and {EMAIL} sends its notification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source checking and copying consumed attention, while literature used inconsistent formats. Indicator revisions and definitions were easy to lose in workbooks.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled feeds, revision storage, and chart generation are established techniques. AI coding lowers assembly effort, and bounded extraction reduces the first reading pass.
tasks.still_hard: Paywalls, licensing, revised statistics, seasonal effects, and conflicting definitions remain. A source-supported summary can still omit a weak signal or exaggerate relevance.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which industry changes matter to this business and challenge fashionable narratives with conflicting evidence.

ambition.what: A monthly early-signal briefing for product and campaign planners.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time checking releases and producing charts, leaving more time to investigate weak signals. The analyst can gain authority to place an evidence-backed issue on the planning agenda.

reach.task: Adjust campaign assumptions when market conditions change.
reach.learn: Planning cycles, demand drivers, and the evidence needed to revisit a forecast.

reach.task: Prepare a concise industry bulletin with reliable sourcing.
reach.learn: Source attribution, editorial judgement, and explaining uncertainty plainly.

evidence.claim: Release monitoring, revision tracking, indicator calculations, and chart generation suit deterministic technology.
Bounded literature extraction can prepare cited notes, while business relevance remains a human judgement.
The digest documents nonexistent citations in a generated report, supporting passage-level validation.

assumptions: The initial source list is bounded and collection is permitted.
Most numeric releases are available as structured downloads or stable tables.
Difficult document tables remain exceptions rather than silently becoming numeric facts.
The large document-reading share follows the prior; email is only a small distribution step.
This monitoring uses public business information and does not profile individuals.
Source licence costs are separate from the low technical running-cost estimate.
unknowns: Which publications allow automated retrieval and summarisation?
Which indicators have consistent definitions and revision histories?
How many languages and publications must be covered?
Who uses the bulletin to make an actual planning decision?
What access approvals or national consultation obligations apply to the proposed setup?
research_questions: Which existing release alerts can be configured instead of building collectors?
How often do source revisions materially change the reported trend?
Does assisted extraction preserve weak signals as well as headline findings?
new_work: Review cited notes and unresolved reading exceptions.
Maintain source access, indicator definitions, and revision handling.
Tune alert thresholds and retire sources that add little value.
Check whether bulletins reach the relevant planning decisions.
tasks.statement: Monitor industry statistics and follow trends in trade literature.

tasks.short: Choose research methods, design surveys, test questions, and arrange access to existing data.

steps.what: Agree the business question, target population, deadline, and required confidence.
Inspect available datasets, coverage, dates, and existing research.
Resolve source permissions, privacy requirements, and gaps with data owners.
Choose collection method, sampling approach, measures, and analysis limitations.
Draft questions, response options, introductions, and participant information.

loop.input: Collection plan, approved question library, and participant information requirements.
loop.output: Draft questionnaire with question origins and flagged additions.
loop.check: Check required fields and response scales; analyst checks bias, meaning, accessibility, and translations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved questions return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard measures, but new research questions need wording adapted to context.

steps.what: Build the pilot questionnaire in a survey platform.
Test comprehension with pilot participants and assess needed changes.
Approve collection scope, participant contact, and source access requests.
Send approved requests for existing data to source owners.

tasks.design: A source inventory on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feeds collection templates in {DOCS}; a bounded drafting loop prepares questions from approved material. Configure the survey platform in {OTHER} for pilots and use {WORKFLOW} to record clearance and approval before {EMAIL} sends access requests. The analyst chooses the method and conducts participant testing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source permissions and metadata were scattered. Questionnaire design mixed reusable material with methodological judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing survey configuration, metadata queries, and document templates handle much of the preparation. AI coding can reduce the effort of connecting them; a bounded loop can draft context-specific wording.
tasks.still_hard: Sampling bias, poor coverage, misunderstood questions, and data licensing remain. GDPR applies to personal data; employee research may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when available data cannot answer the question and choose an honest, proportionate research design.

ambition.what: A rapid research-design clinic for teams preparing small market tests.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time finding sources and assembling questionnaires, with more time for pilot interviews and sampling decisions. The sponsor can delegate method selection within an agreed research budget.

reach.task: Define the evidence needed before committing campaign spend.
reach.learn: Decision thresholds, experiment economics, and the cost of delaying a campaign.

reach.task: Test whether participants understand survey questions and navigation.
reach.learn: Accessible forms, comprehension testing, and response burden.

evidence.claim: Source catalogues, survey configuration, and templates can automate preparation while methodology remains human.
Questionnaire drafting with a bounded loop is a proposed design, not a documented case in this digest.
The digest documents a report with nonexistent sources, supporting explicit source checks.

assumptions: The company has recurring research requests and some reusable questions.
The pilot uses existing software and approved source licences.
Data access requests do not accept new contracts or authorise purchases.
Time shares are indicative; judgement occupies more time than the gathering prior suggests.
Consultation and access estimates include review and elapsed working days, not only coding effort.
unknowns: Which datasets have usable metadata and approved access?
Does the survey platform support questionnaire imports and versioning?
Who approves participant contact and source access?
Which national consultation requirements apply to employee research?
research_questions: Which repeated research requests can use existing data instead of a new survey?
Which question families can be configured entirely from the approved library?
Does pilot testing find fewer comprehension problems after assisted drafting?
new_work: Review drafted questions and participant information.
Maintain source permissions, question versions, and metadata.
Handle unsupported survey logic and failed data requests.
Record pilot changes and approval scope.
tasks.statement: Devise and evaluate methods and procedures for collecting data, such as surveys, opinion polls, or questionnaires, or arrange to obtain existing data.

tasks.short: Develop and introduce a repeatable procedure for identifying advertising needs.

steps.what: Retrieve sales, audience and campaign performance records.
Combine exports and calculate comparable segment and campaign measures.
Discuss commercial priorities, customer gaps and advertising constraints with stakeholders.
Define evidence requirements, advertising triggers, exclusions and escalation criteria.
Draft the procedure, responsibilities, intake questions and review schedule.

loop.input: Approved template, proposed decision criteria and stakeholder requirements.
loop.output: Draft procedure with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check required sections and criterion coverage mechanically; analyst verifies meaning, responsibilities and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass, capped at 6000 generated tokens; unresolved sections return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but stakeholder language and procedural explanations need contextual drafting.

steps.what: Approve the procedure's scope, responsibilities and decision criteria.
Publish the approved procedure in the shared document store.
Set up advertising request fields, assignments and review reminders.
Review pilot feedback and decide which procedure changes are needed.

tasks.design: A reusable kit accepts exports or approved connections from {CRM}, {ADS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}; deterministic calculations produce a baseline in {BI}. A bounded drafting loop turns agreed criteria into a procedure in {DOCS}, where the marketing manager approves publication. Configure request fields and reminders in {PROJECT}; recommendations create review items without committing advertising spend.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different campaign definitions and disconnected exports made evidence preparation costly. Procedure design also depends on commercial judgement that software cannot settle.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building adapters, calculations and validation checks. Existing approval and template features handle much of the workflow; a bounded model loop assists with prose.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution, sparse segment data and conflicting commercial priorities remain difficult. Connections and metric definitions need maintenance. GDPR and EU AI Act applicability need assessment for the actual use; employee consultation depends on national rules and whether employee data or monitoring enters scope.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when weak demand reflects positioning, product or distribution problems, and challenge an advertising request accordingly.

ambition.what: Monthly advertising-needs review by customer segment

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding evidence and writing procedures, and more time testing whether advertising addresses a real commercial gap. With delegated authority, they can initiate segment reviews; budget approval remains with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Recommend budget shifts between customer segments.
reach.learn: Contribution margins, incremental demand and the manager's investment criteria.

reach.task: Identify unmet search intent that deserves campaign investigation.
reach.learn: Query intent, organic coverage and paid-search measurement limits.

evidence.claim: Export integration, fixed metric calculations and configured approvals can support this procedure; this is a proposed design, not a documented marketing case.
Contextual procedure drafting can use a bounded model loop with source checks and analyst review.
A documented government-report failure involving nonexistent citations supports checking generated references before publication.

assumptions: The company has campaign and sales records, but an analyst still combines exports for cross-channel comparison.
Procedure development happens periodically; the monthly review is a proposed extension.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates for this task, not measured results.
The first version uses aggregate commercial data and does not score employees.
Build ranges cover one team's initial procedure and a small set of data sources.
Consent and access includes permissions, privacy assessment and employee consultation where national rules require it; elapsed waiting can exceed the working-day estimate.
unknowns: Which systems, exports and connection permissions are available?
Are campaign identifiers and metric definitions consistent across sources?
Who can approve procedures, activate request templates and delegate review authority?
How many channels, markets and languages must the first version support?
Does the proposed data use include personal data or employee monitoring?
Which national consultation rules and existing employee agreements apply?
research_questions: Which existing approval, template and reporting features can remove custom development?
Which advertising triggers remain useful when attribution is incomplete?
Can a pilot distinguish advertising needs from product, pricing and distribution problems?
new_work: Review generated procedure text against agreed criteria and source material.
Resolve unmatched campaign identifiers and changed source fields.
Investigate missing data and disputed advertising triggers.
Maintain metric definitions, request templates and access permissions.
Collect pilot feedback and propose revisions for approval.
tasks.statement: Develop and implement procedures for identifying advertising needs.

tasks.short: Brief, coordinate and support trained survey interviewers, checking fieldwork progress and quality.

steps.what: Prepare the fieldwork brief from the approved research protocol.
Brief interviewers, demonstrate difficult questions and answer procedural questions.
Allocate interviewer shifts and sample quotas in the fieldwork tracker.
Check survey collection software for completion totals, quota gaps and missing responses.
Review response samples against research quality criteria and identify issues needing investigation.
Coach interviewers, investigate difficulties and agree corrective actions.
Update the tracker with agreed actions and revised assignments.

tasks.design: Generate the fieldwork brief from approved templates in the {DOCS}, and configure assignment approval and action records in the {WORKFLOW}. Connect survey collection software in the {OTHER} to a {BI} view of quotas and completeness; supervisors retain briefing, quality judgement and coaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: Occasional fieldwork, agency boundaries and inconsistent trackers made a dedicated integration hard to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and workflow rules cover assignments and updates. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of adapting exports and brief templates.
tasks.still_hard: Interview quality depends on context. Access to respondent data and any interviewer monitoring require GDPR assessment and, where applicable, consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Build interviewer confidence, recognise ambiguous answers and distinguish a procedural problem from poor interviewing.

ambition.what: Daily quota recovery decisions during active fieldwork

tasks.altitude: During fieldwork, the analyst spends less time chasing totals and more time investigating sample gaps. Supervisory and research approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Choose whether a sample gap warrants more fieldwork spending.
reach.learn: Sampling bias, marginal research value and fieldwork cost.

evidence.claim: Templates, quota checks and assignment records can use deterministic rules; supervision still requires conversation.
GDPR and applicable national rules must be assessed when fieldwork tools process respondent or interviewer data.

assumptions: Today uses survey collection software, a shared tracker and live briefings.
The pilot covers one fieldwork team and one survey source.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Monitoring covers operational completeness; individual worker scoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Whether interviewers are employees, agency staff or contractors.
Survey export access and respondent data restrictions.
Existing assignment features and consultation obligations under national rules.
research_questions: Which survey collection interfaces support quota and completeness exports?
Which documented fieldwork cases show less coordination effort without weaker sample quality?
new_work: Review generated briefs and proposed assignments.
Investigate stale feeds, quota alerts and disputed quality findings.
Maintain questionnaire mappings, access permissions and retention settings.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts from collecting, reconciling and formatting evidence toward research design, interpretation and validation. Proposed decision rights cover diagnostic analyses and research prioritisation within an approved scope; managers retain campaign, positioning and investment decisions.
reach: Marketing manager: turn research findings into testable positioning choices.
Search marketing strategist: connect consumer language with search intent.
Online merchant: translate demand evidence into assortment experiments.
Editor: make uncertainty and implications clear to decision makers.
skills_to_grow: Sampling, questionnaire design and qualitative interviewing.
Metric definitions, data quality and reproducible analysis.
Causal reasoning and controlled experiment design.
Source verification and evidence-based writing.
GDPR-aware research operations and data minimisation.
Evaluating assisted drafting and text coding.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a rolling market-evidence service that connects customer behaviour, consumer research and competitor changes to a prioritised validation agenda, with explicit uncertainty and recorded decisions.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward research design, evidence quality, and interpretation as collection and reporting consume less of the week. With explicit delegation, the analyst can initiate market and satisfaction reviews within agreed scope; budget and personnel decisions remain with their accountable owners.
reach: Marketing managers: turn market evidence into campaign and positioning choices.
Online merchants: understand offer equivalence and commercial price comparisons.
Human resources specialists: design trustworthy employee listening and confidential reporting.
Editors: communicate sourced findings and uncertainty clearly.
Web and digital interface designers: improve survey comprehension and accessibility.
skills_to_grow: Sampling, survey design, and nonresponse assessment.
Experiment design and commercial decision thresholds.
Data definitions, revision tracking, and deterministic validation.
Source licensing, GDPR, and national employee consultation requirements.
Reviewing model extraction against original evidence.
Facilitating decisions when evidence is incomplete or contested.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a research service combining a rapid design clinic, weekly competitor-response recommendations, quarterly customer satisfaction reviews, and monthly early-signal briefings. Earn authority to initiate focused research and planning reviews, supported by traceable evidence and clear approval limits.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from collecting and formatting evidence toward research design, forecast challenge and commercial advice. Managers retain spending and strategy approval; interview supervisors retain people leadership.
reach: Help advertising and promotions managers design budget experiments.
Help marketing managers compare launch, pricing and distribution options.
skills_to_grow: Experiment design and causal inference
Data reconciliation and metric definitions
Forecast validation and uncertainty
Sampling quality and fieldwork coaching
Commercial economics and decision communication
GDPR-aware data handling and source verification
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a small market evidence service that combines current campaign results, validated demand scenarios and commercial options clinics for product teams.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward diagnosing demand gaps and designing useful commercial reviews. Decision rights expand only where the marketing manager delegates review initiation or recommendation authority.
reach: Marketing manager: evidence for segment budget allocation.
Search marketing strategist: unmet intent and channel coverage.
skills_to_grow: Incrementality and attribution limits
Commercial diagnosis and contribution margins
Metric definition and data validation
Stakeholder interviewing and procedure design
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a monthly segment opportunity review that identifies whether advertising, positioning, pricing or distribution deserves the next investigation.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
